newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela raises monthly minimum wage 44 percent.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela raises monthly minimum wage 44 percent.

text.p: The Venezuelan government announced Wednesday that it was raising the minimum monthly salary via new subsidies to 75,000 bolivars ($156) per month, an increase of more than 44 percent.

"This new subsidy assures Venezuelan workers a minimum monthly income of about $150, which is above the current income in other countries in the region with similar economic and social conditions," a presidential palace statement said.

The minimum monthly salary had stood at about 53,000 bolivars ($110). The salary rise, through a so-called "bridging bonus," would apply until Congress had approved a series of reforms to Venezuela's social security system, the statement said.
Once the new social security legislation has been approved, the bonuses would be converted into salary.
"The beneficiaries of the subsidy will be private sector workers as the public sector has received substantial increases through collective bargaining," the statement added.
Government workers salaries were raised by about 70 percent earlier this year.

Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni told a news conference the 75,000 bolivar per month salary had been set after taking into account union demands for 90,000 bolivars per month and private sector recommendations for 62,000 bolivars.
Bernardoni said the basic food requirements for a family of five had been estimated at 132,000 bolivars ($275) per month.
The increase to 75,000 bolivars, which applies only to urban areas, was roughly in line with market expectations.
The minimum salary in rural areas was raised to 67,940 bolivars ($142) per month.

President Rafael Caldera had said he would not let the May 1 Labor Day holiday pass without the bonus increase to compensate workers while they wait for Congress to approve the wide-ranging Labor Law reforms.
